items.note: S2.2.1 states the signed exchange (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) with scratch restoration, and its sub-steps follow the proof (741-765). They give the eight-row subtract/add/restore schedule, the central coefficient |S∩T| mod 2 or (|S∩T|-1)/2 with side-wire cancellation, and the three-stage composition (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x). It does not give h=100, the complex side-injection coefficient or the wire counts W_b, W_c (767-782).

It states D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} and the route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} including auxiliary roles. It derives them by the paper's invariant: the stored array is D_v of the logical array, and a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate (804-822).

The statement is complete: nondegenerate labels, triple lines orthogonal for neighbours, only central 3->4 edges decreasing with loss h, L=Ich, total Wm-2N+2L, ratios 100/539 and 101/539, orthonormal residual bases. The derivation gives the terminal sums, stage transitions, central loss and telescoping. It never gives the gate-label table (975-988) or the edge residual table (1021-1043), so the side-wire chain P⊗<t_X> ⊂ P⊗t_Y^⊥ (where neighbour orthogonality is used, 1048-1060) and the check that every other edge is nondecreasing are only asserted (S2.2.3.7).

It has the endpoint identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m, the shear H<-H+D on every role, and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m. These come by the paper's route: rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, the N source exceptions 2P_{U_a} of rank one, and deficit N-2L_b. Calling the projections 'frames' is loose (the frames are the shears Phi_{P_U}), but S3.3 and S3.3.3 supply Phi_M.

It states C_U, one kernel aI+bX_v (or inverse) per orthonormal residual vector, s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c<W_c m and C^{⊗m} on every role on k columns. The derivation follows the proof step by step: weight additivity mod 4, odd weight, H diag(1,-1) H=X, the 27-coordinate exception on X_a->Y_a, the Z_{a,k} and i^{27k} correction, and negating the X outputs.

The chain L/N<1/2 -> deficits N-2L_b>0 and 2N-2L_c>0 -> s<Wm is present. So is 'deficits exceed 20·2^-50 and m^{1-2^-50}>m(1-20·2^-50)' -> s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^-50. The exact relative deficits eta_b=339/22587335000000 and eta_c=73/19906842167500 are never given, and log m<20 is only implicit in the displayed inequality.

S1.1 and S1.2 state the O(V) digit permutations, digit moves, split/merge, cyclic row split into W streams, controlled shift with b^{O(1)} offset and unit multiplication, on a fixed number of tapes. They are presented as citable facts with no derivation (the method is 'state ... once').

Both the factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2 and the cost (exactly rank(A) interchanges plus O(V)) are stated. The cost derivation follows 1425-1446: triangular parts by controlled shifts, one interchange per one of Pi. The condition that q is a fixed odd prime avoiding the table's denominators and diagonal numerators (1397, 1413-1423) is missing. The factorization's elimination proof (topmost row, rightmost pivot, 1375-1392) is absent, since S3.1 is a bare infer step.

The steps follow the proof: the cyclic row split into W role streams (row count divisible by W^{k-1}), Phi_{A_e} edges by recursive interchanges, Phi_{I_m} at the endpoints giving H<-H+D on every row, three componentwise updates for the interchange, s calls on volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) with the two-case geometric sum, and the fixed-tape parking schedule.

S3 states the O(V u^tau) interchange of two u-bit chunks. S3.4 has the row field from rho=O(log e) high digits padded to a multiple of W^k, the base-m pieces, the sum O(V)Σ a_j m^{j tau}=O(V e^tau) and the binary padding. It omits that the high digits h^+, d^+ are themselves interchanged pair by pair and joined, then separated again (1660-1683, 1708-1712). Without that the full chunks are not exchanged.

It has the edge as a product of directional kernels, conjugation by P_M placing directions in slots (one child of C^{⊗f} per direction), the inverse via (C^{-1})^{⊗f}=(-i)^f Z^{⊗f}C^{⊗f}Z^{⊗f}, exactly s_c children on e/m axes giving C^{⊗e} on every role, and H_0^{⊗D}=b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D. These are the paper's steps. The reduction of P_M to a fixed number of row additions appears only through S4.6.5.

It states the packed XOR by whole-chunk cyclic shifts, the address-determined bad set of density at most 80(f-1)2^{-K} with repair by sorting, and the change-of-basis cost O(V((eK)^tau+1)). The lemma's full time bound and the family conditions (K/log p->∞, R superpolynomial) are missing. The derivation has the eight additions, guard interval, union bound and radix-sort repair. It omits the chunk swaps that place each rotation's target (2117-2155, the source of the L^tau cost) and the argument that S_0 and T_0 both preserve B, so T_0S_0^{-1} permutes B and the sort keys are the hole ranks (2107-2114, 2182-2185).

The steps match 2286-2448: q_0 preprocessed chunks as a row index of range at least W^{k_0}, the u=Wg+w role split giving children of volume V/W, F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with leaves O(e) for e<d^beta, internal sum O(e^lambda) via K<=e^{c/beta}, leaves O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}), and the base-m pieces giving O(d^{lambda'}) under the stated condition on lambda'.

It states the D-chunk H_0 layer returned as Q_p(Hz) in O(V d^{lambda'}) with error <√2·2^{-p}, evaluated exactly with one truncation. The guard bound follows the paper: A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E, E=64(W+m+1)^3, sx+E<=(s+E)x, C_0 d^{C_1}=o(p). The uniformity check of the packed lemma's extra terms over the d,r bands (2714-2735) is not shown.

It has omega_t=y^{2r/t}, character cancellation by the shift t/2^{v+1}, DIF with bit-reversed storage and reversed rounds giving B_tF_t^- and F_t^+B_t^{-1}, the grouped twiddle J_E, and the layout L (prefix moves, at most Dq-1 width-K exchanges). It also has the exact counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1} and the cost O(Tp[dK+pK^{tau-1}+l d^{lambda'}]). All follow the paper.
It states evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, four integer products with the established multiplier, centered residues (|h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2), reduction mod y^r+1 and O(rp log(rp)) time, as in 3236-3335.

It has two forward transforms kept in the common LB order (it commutes with pointwise products), packed products, the opposite transform and the scale M. It gives the convolution rule with F^+F^-=I/M, the error √2·M(3l+1)2^{-p} from 3delta+eta, and the cost including log(rp).

It states P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA with contractions A,B_0, error <p^2, time O(t p^{3/2+delta} alpha), the tensor form with gamma=2d alpha^2, error <dp^2 and exposure cost O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)). The derivation follows 3601-3697 and 3836-3889. The permutations (P_s u)_j=u_{tj} and (P_t v)_k=v_{-sk}, which are the point of the lemma, are never defined.

It states and checks QF_t u=ā·(a*(ā·u))/T (period t_i, coefficient comparison) and RF^+[(RFu)(RFv)]=(u*v)/S^2. The latter uses the paper's dilation-by-unit identity F^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F^+ and the commutation of permutations with pointwise products. It also gets RF^+ by conjugation.

It gives all fixed exponents, b, p=6b, d, K, T, r, t_i, alpha, gamma and eta, and Tp=Theta(n). It covers the primes via the Rosser-Schoenfeld/HvdH interval count, T/2<S<T by Bernoulli, alpha^4 theta_i>p, the n^{o(1)} search, and degree <S with coefficients <2^{3b}, as in the paper.

It has Phi: x->∏x_i^{mu_i} as a convolution-preserving isomorphism (order S), the triangular digit formula b_i=a_i+mu_i Σ_{j<i}a_jP_j mod s_i, updates for i=d..1 by prefix-controlled cyclic shifts, and the cost O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)). All match the paper.

It shows Theta: x_d->zeta y is well defined, diagonal and isometric, checks the wrap zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, and gets M_C=D_-iota^{-1}M_r(iota D_+f, iota D_+g)=(f*g)/T. It describes the computed twist sequence, but its per-twist error (<4·2^{-p}, used at 4609-4614) is not given.

It has the source transform (A, computed chirp, B_0, 2^gamma), exact counterpart RF_s, and the opposite transform by conjugation. It gives the six steps: digits as numerators a_j 2^{p-b-2}, Phi, two transforms, product, F^+ and scale S, scale 2^{2b+4}S with rounding, Phi^{-1}, carries. It also explains the two occurrences of S. All match 4434-4544.

It chains the disk margins (.701), the chirp error 8TL, E_s=9·2^gamma TL, the product error (2E_s+2), the opposite transform (3E_s+2), E_w<28·2^gamma T^2 L, and the final bound 448b·2^{-b+gamma}<=448b·2^{-3b/4}<1/2. It ends with rounding to the unique integer and the carry recurrence with k_j<Q_0^2. The ring error E_ring<5TL is only implicit.

It has the cost table normalized by Tp, the margins g_1..g_7 with their values, min g_i=g_2=2^{-181}=2kappa, setup and exceptional sorting o(Tp), polylog absorbed by p^kappa, O(Tp·p^{1-kappa})=O(n(log n)^{1-kappa}), and the schoolbook cutoff. All match the paper.

No step states that one machine with liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n)=0 refutes an eventual n lg n lower bound. S0 only lists 'nlogn-conjecture' among its relied-on concepts and its motivation is about the Theta(n log n) scanning cost, so I count it as absent rather than mentioned.

errors.says: Method: the two tape procedures are each 'driven by a finite linear network with total edge rank below its wire count'.
errors.paper: The decisive inequality is s<Wm, total rank below wire count times the dimension m (168, 1468). s is close to Wm and far above W. S2 and S2.2 state it correctly.

errors.says: 'Using the projections P_U onto the labels as frames' the bit network gives the shear H<-H+D.
errors.paper: The projections are the vertex matrices M_v. The frames are the address shears Phi_{M_v}: (H,D)->(H+M_vD,D) (1115-1131, 1504-1517).

errors.says: The top rho digits of each chunk are peeled off as a row index; the remaining width is split in base m and interchanged; then padding is undone and binary ranges are padded to radix q.
errors.paper: The high parts h^+, d^+ are first interchanged digit by digit and joined to form the row field q^{2rho}>=W^k, and are separated again at the end (1660-1683, 1708-1712). The binary padding to [q^e] is the outer wrapper applied first (1721-1734).

errors.says: The packed XOR is done by a constant number of cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges plus a repair. The motivation says chunk interchanges are avoided because they cost too much.
errors.paper: Each of the eight rotations is preceded and followed by a chunk swap (Lemma chunk-swap, O(V L^tau)) that brings its target to the rightmost chunk position. There are up to sixteen swaps, and they are the source of the V L^tau term (2117-2155, 2195).

errors.says: 'Because the sparse Gaussian window has radius ceil(sqrt p)·alpha', the maps S', J', D' cost O(t p^{3/2+delta} alpha).
errors.paper: The time bounds are quoted from HvdH Lemmas 4.8, 4.9 and 4.12, and D' costs O(t p^{1+delta}) (3651-3666). The window radius is used only to bound the tape movement inside the S' procedure (3741-3746).

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound: stream primitives (S1); the two networks with frames, labels and the s<Wm saving (S2); interchange (S3) and the simultaneous layer (S4) by the recurrence; synthetic transforms and convolution (S5); resampling and chirp with retained permutations (S6); parameters, primes, CRT and twist (S7); then assembly, exact recovery and the cost table (S8). It thins out in the label lemma (gate-label and residual tables not given), the factorization proof and choice of q in the matrix shear, the high-digit exchange in the arbitrary-width interchange, and the chunk swaps and B-preservation argument in packed addition. The final disproof clause (liminf argument) is absent.

steps.note: It has the banks indexed by triples of 3-subsets, m=10^6, the fixed network giving (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and restoration of every scratch value. h=100 and N=binom(100,3)^3 are never stated explicitly, though N is used as a symbol.
It has the common frame commuting with a pointwise gate, the implemented operator D_out S D_in^{-1}, and the route cost as a change of frame applied edge by edge.
It has nondegenerate subspace labels in the m-dimensional tensor space (stage labels A⊗<t>⊗Q), comparable labels on every edge, and only the central 3->4 edges decreasing, each by h.
It has rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U for nested labels, with the N source edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one as the only exceptions.
It has the sum of absolute changes Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich, and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
It has L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2, so the deficit N-2L_b>0 (and 2N-2L_c>0) and s<Wm.
It has P_{U_a^⊥}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m on X_a and 0 to I elsewhere, hence Phi_{I_m}: H<-H+D on every role and every row, including scratch rows.
It has A=E_1 Pi E_2, exactly rank(A) interchanges plus O(V) per edge shear, and s recursive calls per node in total.

It has children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), deficits >20·2^{-50} with m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20·2^{-50}) giving s/W<m^tau for tau=1-2^{-50}, and F_k=O(e^tau). log m<20 appears only through that inequality, and the exact eta values are not given.

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the whole central chain: fixed exchange network, frames, labels, rank equals dimension change, the budget Wm-2N+2L, L/N<1/2 giving s<Wm, the endpoint identity giving the shear, edges as rank-many recursive interchanges, and the recurrence with tau=1-2^{-50}. The only gaps are the unstated sizes h=100 and N, and the unverified per-edge label tables.
